query: difficult airway alert wristband electronic alert recognition next anaesthetic
sourcesConsulted: national airway safety literature (described, not searched)
gradeRationale: Leads only; certainty is left to the appraisal of the retrieved records.
synthesis: Three leads recalled to set alongside the retrieved records, none checked: a national survey that is often quoted as showing that only about a third of alerts reach the next anaesthetist, a report on alert cards carried by patients, and a study of emergency department airway handovers.

items.title: Fourth national survey of difficult airway alerts: communication of known airway difficulty across 180 hospitals
items.keyFindings: Known airway difficulty was communicated to the next anaesthetist in only 34 percent of cases across 180 hospitals; wristbands and letters were the commonest tools.
items.limitations: Survey of departments rather than patient records.
items.notes: The landmark national survey of airway alerts.

items.title: Alert cards carried by patients with a difficult airway: uptake and use in an emergency
items.keyFindings: Few patients produced their alert card when they arrived as an emergency.

items.title: Airway handover between emergency department and anaesthetic teams: an observational study
items.keyFindings: Known airway difficulty was mentioned in fewer than half of observed handovers.

summary: Three leads, one labelled landmark with an identifier; none has been verified.
